projects.name: 2023-2025 2.2.5 Adolescents and youth are provided with the opportunities to develop their twenty-first century skills to actively and productively participate in society
projects.description:
As adolescents can significantly contribute to societal development, if equipped with a set of 21st century skills in the area of education, media, digitalization and social life, by working with adolescents, their communities and key institutions, such as schools, to build, promote and support their skills and competencies, it is expected that a critical mass of adolescents will be able to better connect among themselves, mitigate risks and strengthen core social values that the country needs. In parallel with technical support provided to government to build and implement the competency- based curricula, UNICEF will work to increase opportunities to learn business and other skills and competencies trough non-formal education. UNICEF will further invest in awareness raising about the importance of adolescence in the life-course perspective; its linkage with socio-emotional development, behaviour and job readiness. UNICEF will help improve the capacities of government institutions to monitor and evaluate interventions and programmes for adolescents, also using U-Report   to ‘feed’ and test such interventions, to develop core indicators and improve the quality of data and information sharing among all key actors. 

Furthermore, UNICEF will invest in creating more demand in society for skills-based education, by implementing communication for development interventions targeting the general public, including decision-makers, parents/caregivers and CSOs, and emphasizing the importance of skills development for adolescents, including for the most vulnerable groups such as girls, Roma and adolescents with disabilities.

projects.name: 2023-2025 2.1.6 Government and education institutions have enhanced capacities and financial resources to effectively provide quality and inclusive early childhood education and care
projects.description:
To improve the quality and inclusiveness of support to young children, UNICEF will support the government institutions with ECEC teacher education in line with the EU recommendations on High-Quality ECEC Systems which also encompass social model of inclusion of vulnerable groups of children. In addition to in-service training, efforts will be invested to enhance the quality-of-pre-service teacher education, which implies better connections of theoretical learning with practice and shifting university education from a teacher-centered to a child-centered approach. Professional development initiatives will also address potential teachers’ biases towards inclusion and gender and build their self-efficacy to support and promote inclusion. 
To increase demand, UNICEF will work intensively to increase community engagement by gaining a better understanding of communities’ knowledge and attitudes towards ECEC, promotion of the importance of ECEC among parents and caregivers, and to address prejudices towards the inclusion of vulnerable groups of children in mainstream ECEC (e.g. children with disabilities, Roma, children without parental care). The parents, families and communities will be involved in design and implementation of those interventions. UNICEF will work on advocacy and professional development initiatives towards building stronger parent/caregiver-preschool partnership, taking into consideration engagement of fathers and men in ECEC. 
UNICEF will also support the establishment of referral mechanisms which can foster quality inclusion of Roma boys and girls in ECEC, by engaging different local sectors and Roma authorities. It will support ECEC systems to introduce and improve inclusive ECEC education for children with disabilities, by supporting governments in establishing integrated early intervention and detection services and mechanisms as part of ECEC (with endorsement of the ICF and in collaboration with health and social protection sectors), by fostering teacher collaboration which brings services to their natural environments (rather than segregated services) and the usage of community referrals outside preschool institutions themselves. UNICEF will promote the social and human rights-based approaches to inclusion in BiH communities, in close cooperation with key advocates- Roma leaders and DPOs (Disabled Person’s Organizations).

projects.name: 2023-2025 1.2.8 Support economic empowerment of rural women through access to finance, policy and capacity-building measures
projects.description: The Project will address the issue of existing gender economic inequalities from several angles to maximize the intervention’s impact. The Project will be structured in the format of Phase I of the two-phased intervention with the total duration of approximately six years - consecutive Phase II is already envisioned at this stage. Under Outcome 1 the activities will aim at mainstreaming gender considerations into policy-making, as well as institutional budgeting, planning, programming, and monitoring processes, hence establishing the enabling environment for women farmers, women-led agri-businesses, cooperatives, associations and networks. Under Outcome 2 an integrated approach to addressing the problem of rural women’s limited access to economic opportunities taking into consideration strengthening resilience to climate change risks is being developed both from the supply and demand sides. From the supply side work will be done to establish access to finance mechanisms which will be accessible to the primary beneficiaries through the public sector grants and mobilized private sector finance. From the demand side the main objective is to capacitate women beneficiaries through establishing networking platforms and providing all-encompassing training in business and farm management, digitalization and other skills with the use of FAO’s proprietary Farmer Field Schools (FFSs).

projects.name: 2023-2025 1.1.16 Design and implement activities to enhance disaster risk reduction capacities and related measures (Joint UN Programme on DRR, Phase II)
projects.description:
By the end of Phase II, the legislative and institutional frameworks for the establishment and functioning of DRR platforms at each level would be strengthened and state, entity, Brcko District, and at least 14 municipal DRR platforms established, and functioning based on a modality developed during Phase I.

Local-level DRR Platforms (LDRRP) are established to serve as locally-owned DRR coordination mechanisms and capacitated to mainstream DRR into local policies and strategies, and support community resilience-building. The LDRRPs consist of appointed representatives from relevant sectors (protection and rescue, education, social and child protection, health, and agriculture) with mandate to ensure strong local ownership and leadership of the DRR process, based on a shared understanding of DRR with its multi-sectoral and multi-disciplinary nature to contribute to building the community's resilience. State, entity, BD and local DRR Platforms will serve as institutional mechanisms throughout implementation of the Programme activities while at the same time, the Programme will be building their capacities to ensure sustainability of LDRRPs in the long run.

The Program will support development of vertical, horizontal, and inter-sectoral coordination and communication strategies, mechanisms, protocols and tools. Effective coordination of disaster risk reduction from state level to entity, and local platforms will ensure an all-of-government and all-of-society approach to reducing risk and building resilience. Through the established platforms, Programme will support ORR-mainstreamed strategic and action planning frameworks development for state, entity, Brcko District, and local level for all sectors and will ensure multi-stakeholder engagement in building resilience, by implementing ORR measures and mainstreaming risk reduction across relevant sectoral policies, programmes and instruments.

Capacity of local platforms would be strengthened in organizing and controlling day-to-day operational activities, including implementing long-term programmes with flexibility/authority to respond to new localised challenges as they arise. In addition, sectoral Institutions will be strengthened to implement risk reduction/preventative measures.

projects.name: Strengthening Bosnia and Herzegovina’s resilience to address the impact of the Ukraine war on food security and incomes of most vulnerable groups
projects.description:
Having high dependence on fertilizers, natural gas and petroleum from the Russian Federation and moderate dependence on selected agricultural commodities from Ukraine, Bosnia and Herzegovina has already experienced inflationary pressure resulting from the war in Ukraine. According to the IMF, the country's average consumer price inflation is projected to skyrocket and reach 6.5% in 2022, and these increase in poverty and reduced food affordability and possible food shortages will have a disproportionately more drastic effect on the most vulnerable groups in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As this downward economic trend in more limited access to food is projected to deteriorate further, the current meal provision services will need to re-assess their capacities and changes in demand not to leave too many needy behind.

FAO and UNDP are implementing this Joint Programme with the following objectives:
•	Assess the impact of the war in Ukraine on smallholder farmers and agri-food producers’ access to finance, seeds, fertilizers and other agricultural inputs and the resulting effects on the past and projected agricultural outputs.
•	Analyze the degree of the country’s dependence on other import and export markets for key agricultural commodities in the context of the intraregional trade and food security scenarios.
•	Assess food security demand by the most vulnerable as well as map the food centres’ infrastructure and develop concrete recommendations for policy and technical measures that contribute to zero hunger in the country. 
•	Support entity-level institutions and donor partners with evidence-based adaptive contingency planning and emergency response programming in the areas of food security and social protection, with the focus on the access to food by the most vulnerable groups.

These interventions contribute to SDGs 1 and 2, as well as to the UNSDCF Outcomes 1 (Inclusive and sustainable growth) and 3 (Inclusive health and social protection systems).

projects.name: Restored Ecosystems via Sustainable, Integrated Management of land-based resources
projects.description:
The project seeks to address these challenges through a comprehensive and coordinated strategy that aims not only to protect food security, economic resilience, and rural livelihoods but also to reduce the risk of social and political tensions arising from competing claims over resource rights and responsibilities. By adopting an environmental peacebuilding approach, and aligning with the principles of the UNCCD’s Peace Forest Initiative (PFI), the project emphasizes natural resources as catalysts for cooperation rather than sources of conflict, fostering inter-sectoral and cross-entity dialogue to identify common goals that support sustainable resource management alongside broader objectives of social stability and improved livelihoods. To this end, a dedicated Interministerial Working Group will be established and supported, bringing together all key stakeholders at the state, entity, and cantonal levels. 
The project will also support the formal endorsement of critical policies and strategies, such as the Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Roadmap and a 20-year integrated ‘Land and Peace Strategy,’ providing a clear pathway forward and outlining the capacity-building needs required for effective implementation. 
Additionally, the project will pilot innovative agroforestry interventions in two strategic municipalities, Čapljina and Trebinje, to demonstrate the practical application and benefits of the proposed approach. These pilots aim to showcase positive environmental, socio-economic, and potential peacebuilding impacts, which will be documented and disseminated to facilitate broader replication and scaling-up.
Overall, the proposed intervention aims to enhance the capacity, collaboration, and cooperation of BiH institutions in land and natural resource governance, fostering lasting trust between institutions and communities around a shared commitment to integrated resource management. As a result, this is expected to strengthen the resilience of rural communities and natural ecosystems, contribute to peace and security, and advance meaningful progress toward reversing land degradation and achieving Land Degradation Neutrality.

projects.name: 2023-2025 1.2.9 Strengthen technical capacities for development and implementation of policy, strategy and investment programmes on food loss and waste reduction
projects.description:
The project aims at food loss and waste (FLW) reduction in the context of the national food system. In the longer term, this will result in a reduction of the national contribution to climate change, and a mitigation of the pressure on the national food system for increased production demanded by population and income growth, urbanization and changing consumption prefer-ences and patterns. At the same time, the project would contribute to the FLW regional strat-egy that consists on the formulation of national FLW reduction strategies, and training in FLW measurement, analysis, monitoring, accounting and reporting.
The Action will address the following issues: 
1) Lack of hard data of FLW which show in which VCs and where in the VCs the problem is the most pressing, what the impact is and what the causes are. This lack of concrete infor-mation hampers targeted solutions finding and therefore prevents the implementation of a FLW reduction strategy at national level.
2) Lack of skills in measuring, accounting and reporting of FLW at national level. Measuring is essential to know how big the problem is and where, so that policies, strategies and targeted action can be developed.
Project beneficiaries will be trainers, extension specialists and other staff of national institu-tions, government, NGOs and CSOs, as well as farmer/fisher organizations, food processors, retailers, horeca actors and to some extent household consumers. The project will collaborate with and benefit from external international institutions (e.g., UNDP), providing technical ad-vice and knowledge in FLW measurement and accounting, FLW reduction methodologies, and publicity, awareness raising and information dissemination.

The Project will be structured in the format of Phase I of the two-phased intervention with the total duration of approximately six years - consecutive Phase II is already envisioned at this stage. Under Outcome 1 the activities will aim at mainstreaming gender considerations into policy-making, as well as institutional budgeting, planning, programming, and monitoring processes, hence establishing the enabling environment for women farmers, women-led agri-businesses, cooperatives, associations and networks. Under Outcome 2 an integrated approach to addressing the problem of rural women’s limited access to economic opportunities taking into consideration strengthening resilience to climate change risks is being developed both from the supply and demand sides.
